headline_marked: OpenAI unveils [[GPT-5.6 models]] with enhanced AI capabilities
headline: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 models with enhanced AI capabilities
summary: OpenAI launches GPT-5.6 models with improved efficiency and cost-effectiveness. The models are designed for enterprise work, coding, and scientific research.
details: OpenAI has introduced its newest family of models, GPT-5.6, which comes in three variants: Sol, Terra, and Luna. These models expand what users can do across a variety of fields, with the company promising powerful capabilities in enterprise work, coding, and even scientific research.

The GPT-5.6 models are orders of magnitude more efficient and cost-effective than previous versions. Sol is 54% more token efficient when it comes to AI coding tasks. The company calls 5.6 its 'strongest cybersecurity model yet, achieving frontier performance with significantly fewer tokens.'

GPT-5.6 supports defensive activities, including threat modeling, code review and patching, and blue teaming. OpenAI also released a new tool called ChatGPT Work, designed as a workplace companion for enterprise teams.

The models are priced as follows: Sol is $5 input / $30 output, Terra is $2.50 input / $15 output, and Luna is $1 input / $6 output per million tokens. GPT-5.6 is now available across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API.

headline_marked: Playdate helps Big Ben ring on time with [[clock-timing tech]]
headline: Playdate helps Big Ben ring on time with clock-timing tech
summary: Playdate used for non-gaming purpose: clock timing
details: The Playdate, a handheld gaming device, has been used for a unique non-gaming purpose: helping Big Ben's clock tower bells ring on time. Clock mechanic Andrew Strangeway has programmed the Playdate to check the timing of the iconic clocktower's bells.
This is not the first time the Playdate has been used for a non-gaming purpose. An earlier video showed the device being used during preparations at Big Ben to ring in 2025 on New Year's Eve.
Playdate posted about the cameo on Bluesky, highlighting the device's ease of programming and sideloading capabilities.
caption:

The Playdate, a handheld gaming device, has been used for a unique non-gaming purpose: helping Big Ben's clock tower bells ring on time. Clock mechanic Andrew Strangeway has programmed the Playdate to check the timing of the iconic clocktower's bells.
